entries.title: Tapis OAuth2 login and WebODM user provisioning
entries.what: Replaces the ordinary interactive login experience with Tapis authorization, callback handling, and creation/update of the corresponding WebODM user.
entries.why: Use TACC identities for access to WebODM and downstream Tapis resources (initial commit explicitly describes Tapis-only authentication).
entries.how: TapisOAuth2Backend, OAuth client/token/state models, authorization and callback views, login templates, admin registration, context processors, and environment-driven client bootstrap. The backend currently decodes JWT claims locally; its name/docstring must not be read as proof of cryptographic signature verification.
entries.check: Preserve identity mapping, state/callback behavior, user permissions, client configuration, and login/logout redirects. Explicitly review JWT verification before choosing what to port.

entries.title: Token normalization, expiration, warning, and reauthentication
entries.what: Warns users before Tapis session expiry, logs them out at expiry, and rejects expired tokens in downstream operations.
entries.why: Prevent requests from continuing with expired credentials and treat expiry as a fresh-login boundary (341bdf94).
entries.how: Token helpers normalize nested access-token payloads, compute effective expiration from stored metadata/JWT claims, and apply an expiry skew. TapisTokenManager checks every 30 seconds and warns within ten minutes. August changes removed the Tapis refresh API/call sites; the legacy refresh_token field remains.
entries.check: Check warning, logout once, malformed/expired tokens, near-expiry background requests, and absence of silent Tapis refresh. Label Studio PAT exchange is a separate mechanism.

entries.title: JWT-aware processing-node API adapter
entries.what: Carries the task owner’s Tapis credential through processing submission, status/output polling, restart, cancel/remove, and result download.
entries.why: Stock processing-node calls did not satisfy the custom ClusterODM authentication contract.
entries.how: JWTNodeWrapper wraps pyodm and supplies the JWT as the token query parameter, with node-token fallback. ProcessingNode methods accept jwt_token and Task resolves the owner’s current stored token. The wrapper handles response compatibility and auth errors.
entries.check: Exercise the entire lifecycle against ClusterODX, including output and ZIP retrieval. Do not assume NodeODX/ClusterODX accepts identical credential transport or response envelopes.

entries.title: Cluster node registration, HTTPS, metadata, and visibility
entries.what: Connects WebODM to the primary cluster and makes it visible to ordinary members of the Default group.
entries.why: Resolve cluster connection, HTTPS, missing metadata, image-limit, and object-permission problems.
entries.how: Connection/setup helpers register the node; ProcessingNode tolerates missing cluster engine fields and unlimited image counts, handles unavailable options, and selects the wrapper on port 443. Boot and node-save hooks grant object visibility for the configured primary cluster.
entries.check: Verify non-admin users can select ClusterODX; compare /info and /options response shapes, engine names, image limits, and HTTPS handling.

entries.title: Authenticated cluster admin shortcut
entries.what: Adds a WebODM shortcut into the cluster administration UI.
entries.why: Allow administrators to reach cluster management using their existing Tapis session.
entries.how: A protected WebODM view retrieves and checks the stored token and renders the cluster redirect template; navbar integration uses CLUSTERODM_URL.
entries.check: Verify superuser-only access, token expiry, destination URL, and the ClusterODX admin authentication contract.

entries.title: Tapis flight discovery and project creation
entries.what: Discovers accessible ptdatax.project.* systems and flight image directories, then creates flight-tagged WebODM projects/tasks.
entries.why: Reduce manual project setup for imagery already organized in Tapis storage.
entries.how: TapisStorageService searches Systems/Files APIs for <Flight>/code/images, constructs project metadata, and checks existing owner/tags to avoid duplicate projects. APIs and a management command expose discovery. The automatic _schedule_image_download method only logs a TODO; automatic end-to-end import is not established.
entries.check: Validate real storage layout, API request/response compatibility, duplicate handling, task creation, and which image-download path is actually invoked. Do not mark discovery-to-processing as complete from project creation alone.

entries.title: Discovery preferences and background task support
entries.state: Present configuration/task code; wiring needs validation
entries.what: Stores per-user discovery preferences and exposes controls plus discovery/download/sync/cleanup Celery tasks.
entries.why: Make discovery opt-in and limit repeated scans and project creation.
entries.how: TapisUserPreferences stores login discovery, limits, cooldown, notification preferences, and preferred systems. Callback code can enqueue discovery with synchronous fallback; preference/control APIs and Celery tasks supply the supporting operations. Persisted notification options do not prove notification delivery exists.
entries.check: Verify cooldown/limits/system filters at actual execution points, Celery registration and scheduling, manual synchronization, and whether each exposed preference has a working consumer.

entries.title: Server-side file/directory import browser
entries.what: Lets users browse server imports and import existing task assets or create a new unprocessed task from a directory of source images.
entries.why: Use imagery already on server/Corral storage without sending it through the browser again.
entries.how: TaskAssetsImport normalizes relative paths under the configured imports root and uses path traversal checks. Source-image imports recurse, resolve duplicate basenames, hard-link or copy files, copy recognized GCP files, and create a partial task for later configuration. Asset directories can be zipped for the existing import flow.
entries.check: Check permissions, root confinement, image versus result import, duplicate names, nested folders, GCP handling, and later commit/processing of the partial task.

entries.title: Shared-filesystem submission to processing nodes
entries.what: Submits the task directory as import_path instead of uploading individual image bodies to the cluster.
entries.why: Avoid redundant transfer of large image collections already accessible from the processing environment.
entries.how: When WO_SHARED_VOLUME_ROOT is configured, Task passes its directory, ProcessingNode maps MEDIA_ROOT-relative paths into the shared root, and JWTNodeWrapper calls the path-based creation API. This is distinct from both the server import picker and browser folder upload.
entries.check: Verify container-to-Corral path mapping and ClusterODX import_path support, missing directories, root confinement, and multipart submission with shared mode disabled. Code fallback paths are not proof every fallback succeeds.

entries.title: Browser folder upload and chained folder selection
entries.what: Adds directory selection alongside file selection; successive picker invocations allow several directories to be added.
entries.why: Make large flight uploads easier while retaining the ordinary upload pipeline.
entries.how: A webkitdirectory input filters accepted files and feeds Dropzone’s existing addFile/addedfiles events. The picker reopens after a successful selection; Cancel ends the chain.
entries.check: Check supported browsers, Cancel, unsupported files, duplicate names, GCP files, progress, and chunked uploads.

entries.title: Large-image limits and temporary-directory resilience
entries.what: Raises Django upload memory thresholds and creates task/upload temporary directories before file operations.
entries.why: Support drone imagery and avoid failures after fresh media mounts or missing temporary directories.
entries.how: Settings raise FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE and DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE to 100 MB; task file operations ensure relevant directories exist. These are request/memory thresholds, not a documented unlimited-upload guarantee.
entries.check: Verify large and chunked image/GCP uploads after a clean mount, permissions, and new upstream upload-limit behavior.

entries.title: TAS allocation lookup and processing controls
entries.what: Lists active allocations for the current user and provides allocation, runtime, node-count, and queue inputs in task configuration.
entries.why: Submit TACC workloads with valid accounting information and appropriate resources.
entries.how: A TAS service-account client filters active projects/resources, deduplicates charge codes, chooses a default, and exposes a user API. EditTaskForm loads allocations and inserts the scheduling options; Compose propagates TAS configuration to application services.
entries.check: Verify user-to-TAS mapping, active allocations, API failures, selected charge code, and option names accepted by the new cluster/LS6 path.

entries.title: Allocation-based access control and caching
entries.what: Restricts selected project/task write operations to users with an approved active allocation.
entries.why: Prevent unauthorized uploads and job submissions without repeatedly querying TAS for each chunk.
entries.how: HasRequiredAllocation applies to project creation and task create/upload/commit. An empty required-allocation list disables the gate; superusers bypass it. Enabled checks fail closed on configuration/service errors. Charge-code results are cached, with a configurable lifetime defaulting to the WebODM JWT lifetime.
entries.check: Check allowed/denied users, expired/revoked allocations, outage behavior, superuser bypass, and actual action coverage; current guard placement is not proof every write endpoint is covered.

entries.title: Cluster-aware categorical processing options
entries.what: Renders categorical processing options and cluster destinations as selectable values instead of unsuitable free-text controls.
entries.why: Handle cluster option metadata and stringified enum domains consistently.
entries.how: PresetUtils normalizes known categorical domains, parses serialized lists, preserves current values, and injects discovered cluster URLs; preset/task forms pass cluster-node information.
entries.check: Compare new ODX option domains and stage names; preserve unknown existing values and verify cluster URL selection.

entries.title: Customized default and LS6 Small processing presets
entries.what: Provides tuned default processing and an LS6 Small preset with scheduling/allocation settings.
entries.why: Offer repeatable processing profiles for the deployed HPC environment.
entries.how: Boot creates/updates system presets with DSM/DTM/classification, quality/resolution, split/merge, concurrency, cluster URL, allocation, runtime, node-count, and queue settings. Default uses three nodes/normal; LS6 Small uses one node/vm-small.
entries.check: Review every option against ODX, especially sm-cluster, split/merge, queue, concurrency, hard-coded destination/allocation, and bootstrap overwrite behavior.

entries.title: Offline/missing-task restart fallback
entries.what: Attempts restart with the existing task UUID and falls back to creating a replacement when restart fails, while treating expired authentication separately.
entries.why: Recover tasks whose processing node or retained remote task is unavailable.
entries.how: Task.process restart handling passes the owner JWT, separates authentication expiry from other failures, and sets the reprocessing path when necessary. The main Restart button now passes rerunFrom=null, requesting restart from the beginning; explicit stage choices remain in its submenu (2805c9cd).
entries.check: Exercise restart on surviving, purged, offline, and expired-token tasks; distinguish resubmission from true checkpoint restoration in the external LS6 worker.

entries.title: Duplicate submission guard
entries.what: Reduces simultaneous duplicate processing submissions by different Celery workers.
entries.why: Slow cluster requests could outlive the existing task lock and permit a second submission (commit rationale).
entries.how: A second Redis SET NX lock named task_submit_<id> surrounds task.process with a 120-second TTL and finally cleanup. Redis errors allow best-effort processing without the extra guard.
entries.check: Check concurrent workers, submissions exceeding TTL, cleanup, and Redis outage behavior; this is not an exactly-once guarantee.

entries.title: Celery initialization and task discovery restructuring
entries.what: Moves the Celery application setup into the worker package and exposes a compatibility module.
entries.why: Resolve initialization/import problems in background processing and support Tapis tasks.
entries.how: worker/__init__.py configures the app, result handling, schedules, autodiscovery, and explicit Tapis-task import fallback; worker/celery.py re-exports the app and mock result helper.
entries.check: Verify which Celery entry point actually loads schedules and all tasks, and prevent duplicate app/scheduler setup when reconciling upstream.

entries.title: Interactive distance measurement
entries.what: Adds a ruler workflow with multiple points, live distance, finish/cancel/clear controls, and a retained summary.
entries.why: Measure distances directly on orthophoto/maps (intent inferred from implementation).
entries.how: Map.jsx manages a Leaflet measurement layer, click/double-click/Escape state, segment distances, and metric plus selected-unit display; Map.scss styles controls and labels.
entries.check: Check multi-segment measurements, units, zoom/pan interactions, double-click finish, Escape, clear, and read-only/public maps.

entries.title: Temporary WMS and XYZ tile overlays
entries.what: Lets users add external WMS or tile layers to a map and adjust their visibility/ordering controls.
entries.why: Compare imagery with other map services without creating a permanent project integration.
entries.how: TemporaryMapLayerDialog validates layer settings; Map constructs Leaflet layers and LayersControlLayer supplies controls. A follow-up changes layer placement.
entries.check: Check WMS parameters, XYZ URL templates, layer order, opacity/removal, external-service failures and CORS; do not assume persistence across reloads.

entries.title: Raster tile/metadata caching and CPU-load reductions
entries.what: Reuses expensive raster metadata/tile responses and reduces concurrent raster computation.
entries.why: Address slow public-map requests from thread oversubscription, repeated rendering, and HiDPI tile amplification (commit bodies).
entries.how: Thread-pool caps are configured in Compose; imagery layers disable detectRetina. Tiler cache keys incorporate raster mtime, relevant query/output parameters and crop geometry, excluding random cache-busting input; TTL is seven days. Cache failures are treated as misses/skipped writes; follow-ups addressed unpicklable values.
entries.check: Verify cache invalidation after reprocessing/crop changes, variant separation, Redis failures, serialization, and concurrency under the upgraded raster stack.

entries.title: EPT-first point-cloud loading with legacy fallback
entries.what: Loads entwine_pointcloud/ept.json when available and otherwise loads legacy potree_pointcloud/cloud.js.
entries.why: Support streaming large point clouds while retaining access to older task outputs.
entries.how: ModelView.pointCloudSource probes EPT, loads it through Potree, and passes the loaded cloud onward; the legacy path loads later. Scene saving is guarded until a viewer exists. EPT support already existed in upstream; this entry describes the fork’s changed loading/control sequence.
entries.check: Test EPT, legacy cloud.js, missing/corrupt clouds, scene save/restore, and the new upstream viewer implementation. Preserve behavior without blindly transplanting loader internals.

entries.title: HTTP byte-range asset responses
entries.what: Serves requested portions of assets using HTTP 206 and range/content-length headers.
entries.why: Originally introduced for Potree v2 streaming; the HTTP helper remained after that viewer experiment was removed.
entries.how: download_file_response parses start/end and suffix byte ranges and yields bounded chunks from the file.
entries.check: Check start/end/suffix and invalid/unsatisfiable ranges against upstream behavior, large assets, authorization, and resource cleanup; do not infer complete RFC compliance.

entries.title: Potree v2 experiment and subsequent removal
entries.what: History added metadata.json/Potree-v2 preference and then explicitly removed it.
entries.why: Record an abandoned experiment so it is not mistakenly counted as a feature that must be restored.
entries.how: February viewer/template commits iterated on format loading; 73432709 removes v2 functionality. Current loader uses EPT and legacy cloud.js.
entries.check: Treat the latest upstream format/viewer choice as a new compatibility decision; retain old-output readability rather than reviving removed code by default.

entries.title: Upstream sensor connections and 2D overlays
entries.what: Connects a WebODM project to an Upstream sensor service and displays campaign/station measurements alongside imagery.
entries.why: Bring environmental sensor context into the imagery workflow.
entries.how: A coreplugin stores project connection settings in GlobalDataStore, probes a fixed list of known API stacks, proxies campaigns/stations/measurements using the user Tapis token, and renders map controls/overlays. Login guidance is supplied when no token is available. Discovery is not arbitrary enumeration of all Tapis Pods.
entries.check: Verify project permissions, service selection/config persistence, login guidance, measurement rendering, and updated upstream plugin hooks.

entries.title: Upstream sensor overlay in the 3D viewer
entries.what: Adds sensor context and time controls inside the point-cloud viewer.
entries.why: Compare station measurements with the reconstructed site in three dimensions.
entries.how: A new Model plugin API hook fires when viewer controls can be added. The sensor plugin converts WGS84 positions into local model coordinates using georeferencing offsets and proj4, and supplies time/measurement display controls.
entries.check: Verify hook timing, coordinates, georeferencing asset paths, time selection and cleanup with the upgraded 3D viewer.

entries.title: Agent-assisted dataset metadata and publishing conversation
entries.what: Adds a task-level CKAN publishing panel that prepares metadata, starts a DSO agent conversation, accepts user edits, and requests confirmation.
entries.why: Reduce manual catalog entry while retaining a user review step.
entries.how: The plugin derives title/notes/tags/temporal coverage/spatial metadata from task assets and user context, calls the DSO agent with the user Tapis credential, and stores conversation/publish state. Follow-ups repair timeouts, source URL instructions, phase messages and error reporting.
entries.check: Check metadata accuracy, report URL access, agent contract, confirmation, timeouts/error recovery and configured enablement. Validate external publishing only under separate approval.

entries.title: Published resource links, visibility, and republish tracking
entries.what: Publishes selected downloadable assets plus map/3D links and records the resulting CKAN dataset URL.
entries.why: Make catalog resources reachable and permit subsequent publishing to reuse the correct organization.
entries.how: Resource generation uses the externally reachable/request-derived WebODM base URL and public viewer routes; publishing makes the task public. Task.ckan_url is stored through migration 0047 and exposed read-only. Plugin state retains owner_org and asynchronous apply/error status.
entries.check: Preserve explicit public-visibility behavior and review it with the user; check anonymous resource/viewer access, asset filtering, URL provenance, organization persistence and republish behavior.

entries.title: Admin-only embeddings panel and site/visit storage
entries.what: Adds a task panel for generating embeddings and labeling tiles, with shared site/visit identifiers and label classes.
entries.why: Organize imagery observations for repeat visits and supervised classification work.
entries.how: A coreplugin exposes task/site/class routes and a React panel, backed by a separate Postgres/PostGIS/pgvector database via psycopg2. API permission and task-button checks restrict current functionality to superusers; task imagery determines the highest-resolution zoom.
entries.check: Verify infrastructure enablement, admin restrictions, task/project permissions, existing site/visit reuse, zoom calculation, new-site naming, and separate database compatibility.

entries.title: Real tile candidates and map-based sample selection
entries.what: Lists imagery-backed tile candidates and lets users select sample tiles geographically.
entries.why: Replace coordinate text entry/placeholders with usable imagery selection.
entries.how: TaskTilesView derives tile grids from raster bounds/zoom; Python/JavaScript tile math helpers and the panel map present selectable tiles linked to site/visit observations.
entries.check: Check grid/bounds/zoom alignment, candidate imagery, coordinate conversions, selection persistence and large-site performance.

entries.title: Inline label painting, class creation, and eraser
entries.what: Allows labeling inside the task modal using a class palette and drag painting, plus adding classes and clearing mistaken labels.
entries.why: Make sample labeling usable without repeatedly switching tools.
entries.how: Two panel tabs drive label apply/clear endpoints; backend code creates/reuses Label Studio projects/tasks and writes site-scoped labels/observations to embeddingsdb. Follow-ups add the class UI, task-name defaults and eraser.
entries.check: Verify drag behavior, class scope, applying/clearing labels, site separation, errors and synchronization with existing Label Studio tasks.

entries.title: Label Studio authentication and annotation webhooks
entries.what: Creates Label Studio projects/tasks and imports submitted annotations back into embeddings labels.
entries.why: Connect imagery selection with a real labeling service and correct the earlier credential mismatch.
entries.how: The server exchanges the Label Studio PAT for an access token, caches it and retries on 401. Webhook registration/receiver use a per-project HMAC-derived shared secret, throttling and task mappings; later code caps project titles to the service limit. These credentials are separate from Tapis login.
entries.check: Check PAT exchange/expiry, title limits, server-side secret handling, webhook rejection/acceptance, project/task mappings, and annotation ingestion.

entries.title: LS6 embedding generation jobs
entries.what: Queues embedding generation as a Tapis Job on LS6 using the logged-in user’s stored token.
entries.why: The Actor worker pool could not provision the large generation image; moving to LS6 follows the working HPC execution pattern (recorded design decisions).
entries.how: apply_embed_generate builds a Tapis Job referencing the configured app/version and site/visit/encoder/task/tile context. Follow-ups base64-encode MSG, shorten job names to Tapis limits, and correct runtime/payload details. The companion execution code lives outside WebODM.
entries.check: Verify job specification, current app/version, payload, allocation/runtime, imagery access and database writes across repositories. Do not restore the superseded embed-generate Actor path.

entries.title: Embedding job polling and Continue workflow
entries.what: Polls the actual Tapis job and offers continuation after a stopped/incomplete run.
entries.why: Avoid permanently displaying running after LS6 jobs finish or fail; user feedback explicitly preferred real job polling over timeout guesses.
entries.how: Submission stores job UUID by visit in GlobalDataStore. Status queries Tapis getJobStatus; activity timeout is fallback only when UUID/polling is unavailable. The panel stops polling and offers Continue for timed_out. A terminal FINISHED job is not proof every expected tile exists.
entries.check: Test queued/running/terminal/error states, missing UUIDs, auth/network failures and safe resubmission. Cross-check companion job upsert/idempotency before claiming full continuation guarantees.

entries.title: Embeddings workspace, diagnostics, STAC, GeoJSON import and training
entries.what: Registers workspace/diagnostics pages and several future-action routes, but does not implement the full classifier workflow.
entries.why: Capture the intended extension points without treating the design document as proof of delivered functionality.
entries.how: workspace_index/model_diagnostics render placeholder shells. Publish/retract STAC and GeoJSON label import explicitly return not-implemented responses; queue_model_train raises NotImplementedError and lacks a workspace/train endpoint.
entries.check: Preserve or deliberately retire entry points; track unfinished work separately. Do not claim working STAC publishing, model training/inference, or diagnostics from route registration alone.

entries.title: Tapis/Corral deployment bootstrap and configuration
entries.what: Automates deployment configuration for the custom Tapis, cluster and Corral environment.
entries.why: Make the integrated deployment reproducible and reduce manual setup errors.
entries.how: setup.sh plus OAuth bootstrap/entrypoint scripts coordinate environment/configuration, mounts, accounts/permissions, reverse proxy/SSL setup, node connection and startup. Boot can upsert the OAuth client from configured environment values. Historical .env/certificate/cookie artifacts also exist and are not feature requirements.
entries.check: Review scripts against current infrastructure docs before execution, preserve required configuration names/mounts, and avoid replaying historical secrets/certificates or running setup during inventory review.

entries.title: Corral service-account ownership and group inheritance
entries.what: Runs media-writing application/worker processes as the configured service UID/GID and keeps shared files group writable.
entries.why: Avoid nobody-owned files and permissions failures on root-squashed Corral NFS.
entries.how: gosu privilege drop uses WO_RUN_AS_USER, numeric UID:GID support, umask 002, setup ownership/group inheritance and throttled permission sweeps. Plugin build directories are made writable before dropping privileges. Nginx group membership is made persistent across worker forks.
entries.check: Verify ownership of uploads, task outputs, cache/logo and rebuilt plugins on the actual mount; check numeric group propagation and nginx reads after restart.

entries.title: Corral-safe backups, opt-in scheduling, and operator control
entries.what: Provides database/media backups and a separate control script for installation, scheduling, execution, status and removal.
entries.why: Avoid wedging Corral with overlapping or same-mount backup I/O and allow backup maintenance without full setup.
entries.how: Backups stage dumps/media locally before pushing snapshots to Corral, use locks/timeouts/retention/logging and bounded mount preflight, and run as the current user. Cron installation is opt-in through WEBODM_ENABLE_BACKUP_CRON; backup-ctl supports explicit enable/disable and db-only runs.
entries.check: Review backup destinations, local capacity, ownership, retention, failed mounts, stale locks and restore procedure. Inventory did not run backups or inspect deployed cron state.

entries.title: Nginx logging, compression, worker and status tuning
entries.what: Adjusts proxy worker behavior, request logging/compression and local status inspection.
entries.why: Improve serving behavior and visibility during public-map and asset workloads (intent partly inferred).
entries.how: nginx.conf.template sets worker_processes auto, accept_mutex, detailed access logs, gzip types and loopback-only nginx_status. Related history pins an nginx image and fixes mount-group behavior.
entries.check: Check proxy headers/timeouts, asset delivery, status access restriction, compression, image compatibility and shared-mount reads.

entries.title: Custom source builds and update behavior
entries.what: Builds the customized WebODM image locally instead of replacing it with the public stock image during update.
entries.why: Keep fork-specific integrations present after webodm.sh update (a0473f2f).
entries.how: webodm.sh update invokes the build path; Dockerfile/Compose include custom dependencies, plugin builds and an app build target. Dockerignore excludes runtime/media/local-dev state. Locale and processing submodule references are pinned/updated in later commits.
entries.check: Verify update/build produces the customized image, worker uses the same source, plugin assets exist, and submodule pins resolve. Do not run stock update blindly on this fork.

entries.title: Database/runtime dependency compatibility
entries.what: Adapts dependencies/settings to Tapis integration and the separate newer embeddings database.
entries.why: Resolve tapipy/PyJWT compatibility and psycopg2/libpq/Postgres SSL and timezone failures documented in commits.
entries.how: History pins PyJWT 1.7.1, raises psycopg2-binary to 2.9.9, and patches Django 2.2 utc_tzinfo_factory for timedelta offsets. Settings tolerate newer tzlocal APIs; Dockerfile contains custom system/runtime dependencies.
entries.check: Reevaluate adaptations against new Python/Django/JWT/GDAL versions; preserve the behavior need rather than blindly retaining obsolete monkeypatches/pins.

entries.title: Isolated local connected stack and restart smoke harness
entries.what: Runs a disposable WebODM → ClusterODM → NodeODM stack with connectivity checks and a restart smoke script.
entries.why: Test control-plane/restart flows without production Corral or Tapis.
entries.how: local-dev Compose/scripts build the fork image, bind offset ports to localhost, persist isolated state, register the local node and support low-memory smoke profiles. Debug-gated WO_LOCAL_DEV_SKIP_AUTH creates/authenticates a localdev superuser. June/October commits improve startup and routing/restart handling.
entries.check: Adapt the harness to ClusterODX/NodeODX, preserve localhost/debug safeguards, and keep real LS6 checkpoint validation separate from local node restart checks.

entries.title: Project intelligence and fork CI workflow removals
entries.what: Adds OpenWolf/Claude project guidance and removes inherited public Docker publishing/test workflows.
entries.why: Maintain project-specific context; the precise reason for deleting inherited workflows is not recorded in the short remove-actions commit.
entries.how: .wolf and .claude contain project memory/hooks; 5b8c8622 deletes .github/workflows/build-and-publish.yml and test-docker.yml. These are contributor/automation changes, not end-user application functionality.
entries.check: Keep project memory read-only during upgrade unless asked; deliberately choose replacement test/build CI and image ownership rather than restoring upstream publishing credentials/targets.

entries.title: Prior 3.1.2-era upstream reconciliation and migration preservation
entries.what: Merges cached old upstream into the custom branch and resolves migration-number collisions without replacing existing fork migrations.
entries.why: Bring core WebODM forward while retaining OAuth models, preferences, CKAN field, and integrations.
entries.how: c79c488e merges a4501835. Upstream Profile.cluster_id, Redirect and Task.wkt migrations are carried as 0048/0049/0050 after fork 0047; initial Tapis migration/merge history remains. Later commits adjust tests, local stack and locale revision. These schema features originate upstream, while their reconciliation/order is custom.
entries.check: Compare full migration graphs with new upstream, keep applied migrations immutable, test clean and restored databases, and preserve model/data compatibility. Earlier recorded test results are historical evidence, not a fresh validation run.

entries.title: Restore missing application logo after media loss
entries.what: Restores the default application logo when a settings record survives but its media file is missing.
entries.why: Avoid a broken application logo after a wiped/replaced media volume (explicit code comment).
entries.how: Boot checks the existing Setting logo path and writes APP_DEFAULT_LOGO when the path is absent or invalid; file handles are managed with a context manager.
entries.check: Verify startup with existing settings and missing media, fresh settings creation, and preservation of a valid custom logo.

entries.title: Theme color normalization and invalid-value handling
entries.what: Keeps template color calculations from failing on empty/invalid colors and accepts short three-digit hex colors.
entries.why: Avoid template errors from nonstandard theme values (inferred from validation changes).
entries.how: _normalize_hexcolor validates/expands hex values; complementary and scaleby return the original input and log a warning when normalization fails.
entries.check: Check empty, malformed, three-digit and six-digit theme colors, and compare equivalent upstream helpers before porting.

entries.title: Processing UUID visibility and console diagnostics
entries.what: Shows the remote Processing UUID in task details and adds request/output diagnostics useful for correlating cluster activity.
entries.why: Connect the WebODM task a user sees to the task tracked by the remote cluster (intent inferred from display/log changes).
entries.how: TaskListItem conditionally renders task.uuid and logs the output request URL; task API and JWT adapter history add output/path diagnostics. The adjacent Task ID display has upstream provenance and is not claimed as a new fork feature.
entries.check: Verify WebODM ID versus remote UUID display and console correlation; retain useful diagnostics without exposing tokens or sensitive paths in logs.

commits.subject: Add Tapis OAuth2 authentication integration
commits.body: Implements Tapis-only OAuth2 authentication for WebODM, disabling all other login methods. Adds new models, API endpoints, admin classes, views, templates, and context processors for Tapis OAuth2; updates environment configuration, Dockerfile, and settings; modifies URL routing and login template to support the new flow. Includes deployment and integration documentation.

commits.subject: Add JWT token support for ClusterODM integration
commits.body: Introduces JWTNodeWrapper to enable JWT token authentication for ClusterODM nodes, updates ProcessingNode and Task model logic to pass JWT tokens when available, and adds TapisUserPreferences model. Also increases file upload limits to 100 MB for drone images and updates migrations to reflect these changes.

commits.subject: Make the nightly backup cron opt-in (WEBODM_ENABLE_BACKUP_CRON)
commits.body:
setup_backup installs a corral-safe backup script (flock + preflight + timeout +
throttled rsync), but it also auto-scheduled the 0 2 * * * cron on every run.
Silently (re)enabling the nightly job -- e.g. during a cutover while corral is
being stabilized -- is an operational foot-gun (see the 2026-06-17 corral I/O
incident, where stale/old backup jobs stacked in D-state and jailed the mount).

Now the script is always installed, but the cron is scheduled only when
WEBODM_ENABLE_BACKUP_CRON=1 is set. Default runs no longer touch the crontab, so
setup.sh can be re-run safely without re-scheduling backups; you enable the cron
deliberately once corral is healthy.

Refs In-For-Disaster-Analytics/WebODM#4, docs/incidents/2026-06-17-corral-backup-io-outage.md

using it just to (re)install or toggle the backup is heavy and risky. This adds a
focused, idempotent control script:

- run: foreground run for testing. status: install/cron/log/alert + any D-state
  backup processes wedged on corral. uninstall: remove cron + script + logrotate.

to this script so there is a single source of truth (noted in the PR).

commits.subject: Backup: run as current user (not sudo) + lock-path fallback
commits.body:
`backup-ctl.sh run` used `sudo`, which runs the backup as root. On corral that is
wrong: root is squashed to `nobody` (backups would be nobody-owned again), and it
diverges from the nightly cron, which runs as the unprivileged user (different
$HOME staging dir and lock ownership -> the observed
`/var/lock/webodm-backup.lock: Permission denied`).

- run: execute the backup as the current user; warn (don't sudo) if invoked as root.
- lock: try /var/lock, fall back to /tmp so directory permissions can't block the
  run. Overridable via WEBODM_LOCK.

The backup needs no root: docker exec works via docker-group membership, and corral
writes should be owned by the service user, not nobody.

Refs In-For-Disaster-Analytics/WebODM#4

commits.subject: Backup media: stage to local disk first, then push to corral (no read+write on same mount)
commits.body:
The media step rsynced corral -> corral, reading and writing the same NFS mount at
once. On slow corral that wedges rsync in uninterruptible (D) I/O -> Ctrl+C can't
stop it and the mount gets saturated (the corral-jail pattern).

Rework it to the same shape the DB dump already uses -- build locally, then move:
- Phase 1: rsync corral -> LOCAL mirror ($WEBODM_STAGE_ROOT/media-mirror), incremental,
  throttled (ionice/nice), time-boxed. Reads corral, writes local (interruptible).
- Phase 2: rsync LOCAL mirror -> corral dated snapshot (--link-dest previous), one pass.
  corral is written but never simultaneously read.

Also:
- Free-space preflight: aborts loudly if local disk can't hold the mirror (accounting for
  the existing mirror), so it can never fill the disk. Override dir via WEBODM_STAGE_ROOT.
- Interrupt trap + run children in the background/wait so Ctrl+C / SIGTERM stop the run
  promptly during local phases.
- `run --db-only` (WEBODM_SKIP_MEDIA=1) for quick tests that skip the heavy media copy.

Refs In-For-Disaster-Analytics/WebODM#4, docs/design/2026-07-01-backup-hardening-corral-safe.md

commits.subject: Backup: hang-tolerant corral preflight (abort instead of wedging on a hung mount)
commits.body:
On a hung `hard` NFS mount, a process wedged in uninterruptible (D) I/O cannot be
killed by timeout/kill -9/traps -- so a plain `timeout`-wrapped corral probe can
itself hang, taking the backup (and an interactive terminal) down with it.

Probe corral in the background with a bounded wait: if it does not return within
PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT+5s, abandon the probe (it may stay in D until corral recovers)
and abort the backup cleanly. The script/terminal is never left hanging; the
main loop uses interruptible sleeps so Ctrl+C works during the wait.

This bounds the "hangs immediately" case (corral down/hung at start). A hang that
develops mid-copy on a hard mount is a kernel limitation no userspace tool can
unwedge; the flock lock still prevents stacking, and such a job clears only on
corral recovery or reboot.

Refs In-For-Disaster-Analytics/WebODM#4, docs/incidents/2026-06-17-corral-backup-io-outage.md

commits.subject: fix(ckan): fix chat timeout and LLM path hallucination in CKAN plugin
commits.body:
Three bugs fixed in the CKAN publish plugin:

1. ChatMessageView was unconditionally calling /resume after propose → END,
   causing 4 rapid <20ms graph invocations with no work done and a frontend
   timeout. Fixed by tracking has_pending_interrupt in GlobalDataStore and
   routing to /resume vs /runs accordingly.

2. apply_ckan_publish (Celery) had the same /resume problem for the final
   apply step. Fixed to use /runs with session_id.

3. ChatStartView sent remote_resources ({url,name,format} dicts) instead of
   source_urls (URL strings), so the agent saw has_data=false. Meta-Llama
   invented placeholder local paths and burned all 6 tool calls on failing
   pdf_summarize calls (~107s total). Fixed by extracting source_urls from
   remote_resources and building an informative message that lists the files
   and explicitly tells the LLM not to call file tools on remote URLs.

commits.subject: Bump psycopg2-binary 2.8.6 -> 2.9.9: old bundled libpq can't handle PG17's direct-SSL negotiation
commits.body:
Root-caused a real, reproducible production failure ("Could not connect to
embeddingsdb: SSL SYSCALL error: Success" from the Generate Embeddings
button), not assumed:

- Raw TCP (nc) and a full TLS handshake (openssl s_client) both succeeded
  from the affected host, ruling out network/firewall/MTU.
- The system's own `psql` (libpq from PostgreSQL 14.23 client tools)
  connected fine with the identical DSN, in the same container.
- The exact same DSN via psycopg2.connect() failed every time with the
  same error.
- `psycopg2.__libpq_version__` reported 110005 -- libpq 11.5, bundled
  inside psycopg2-binary==2.8.6 (~2019-era). embeddingsdb runs Postgres
  17.5, which introduced a newer "direct SSL" connection negotiation using
  ALPN (the embeddingsdb Pod's own logs, seen earlier this session, show
  "received direct SSL connection request without ALPN protocol
  negotiation extension" -- this exact mismatch). A libpq predating that
  feature can't complete the handshake, and reports it as this ambiguous
  SSL_read()-returned-EOF error rather than a clean rejection.

This is WebODM's core DB driver (used for webodm_dev too, not just
embeddingsdb) -- a newer libpq stays backward-compatible with older
Postgres servers, so this is safe for both connections.

instead, matching the shim other Django-2.2-era projects use for this.

commits.subject: Implement real candidate-tile listing, site-scoped labeling, and a Label Studio webhook receiver
commits.body:
Closes out the design spec's "Tile Selection UI" and "Label Studio
Integration: Full Mechanics" sections:

- TaskTilesView: real candidate-tile enumeration (task's orthophoto
  extent + site-zoom-lock-aware effective zoom + real COGReader
  coverage check), for the map-based tile picker.
- TaskLabelView: labeling now gets its own site selector, decoupled
  from whether embed-generate has run (user's explicit choice over
  requiring embedding first) -- creates real tile_grid/tile_observations
  rows on demand instead of sending a placeholder tile_observation_id.
- LabelStudioWebhookView: real webhook receiver. Reviewed by both an
  architect and a security-reviewer before implementing; fixed a
  critical empty-secret fail-open bypass and a high-severity
  cross-project secret-reuse gap (per-project HMAC-derived secrets)
  found during that review, plus a zoom-lock propagation gap that
  would have let labeling and embedding fork one site's tile_grid.
- LabelClassesView: real GET/POST against a new, lazily-seeded
  label_classes query.
- New embeddingsdb table, label_studio_tasks (schema change in the
  sibling embeddings-tapis-actors repo), closing Decision 29's webhook
  scope-validation gap.

Not done here: the actual map UI for tile picking (backend is real,
frontend still takes typed tile ids) and GeoJSON label import.

commits.subject: Replace "Label a Sample"'s text input with a real map-based tile picker
commits.body:
Per the design spec's own "Tile Selection UI: Map, Not a Flat Thumbnail
Grid" section -- deferred as a fast-follow when the backend (GET .../tiles)
was implemented last round, now built:

- A standalone Leaflet map (reusing this plugin's existing webpack
  "leaflet" external, same pattern as coreplugins/objdetect) shows the
  task's own orthophoto as the base layer.
- Candidate tiles from GET .../tiles are drawn as a clickable rectangle
  grid; clicking toggles a tile into/out of the selection. Tiles that
  already have a real tile_observation_id (already labeled or embedded)
  render in a distinct color.
- Refetches whenever the chosen site changes, since a different site can
  have a different locked zoom (and different already-observed tiles)
  for the same task.
- tileMath.js mirrors tile_math.py's bounds formula so the map draws the
  exact tiles the backend computed candidates from.

The map replaces the text input entirely (user's explicit choice) rather
than keeping both.

commits.subject: Label directly in the modal: two tabs, label palette, drag-to-paint
commits.body:
User clarified the goal is to fully integrate Label Studio through
WebODM, not bypass it -- so painting a tile calls Label Studio's real
per-task annotation-creation API (POST /api/tasks/{id}/annotations/)
on the user's behalf, keeping it the true system of record, while the
corresponding `labels` row is upserted immediately rather than waiting
on the webhook round-trip (which still fires and harmlessly re-upserts
the same value).

Backend:
- TaskLabelApplyView (POST .../labels/apply): applies one label_classes
  value to a batch of tiles at once. Validates the value first, creates
  real tile_grid/tile_observations rows, reuses ONE Label Studio project
  across a whole paint session (not one per drag stroke), imports
  not-yet-imported tiles, creates a real annotation per tile, upserts
  labels locally.
- label_studio_client.create_annotation() -- the real per-task
  annotation-creation call (bulk endpoint considered, not used --
  its request shape is ambiguously documented).
- embeddings_client.get_tile_observations_for_visit() (renamed/extended
  from get_tile_observation_ids_for_visit): now also returns each tile's
  CURRENT label value/color, not just observed/unobserved, so the map
  renders real state. get_label_studio_task_id() added for session reuse.
- TaskLabelView (send an unlabeled batch for open-ended human
  annotation in Label Studio's own UI) is kept, untouched -- a distinct,
  still-valid use case, not replaced.

Frontend: modal restructured into "Embedding"/"Labels" tabs. Labels tab
gets a label-class palette (GET .../label-classes) -- clicking a swatch
arms it (map panning disabled while armed), dragging paints every tile
the cursor touches with that label, batched into one apply call on
mouse-up, per the user's explicit "pick label, then paint" preference.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Add "+ Add label class" UI and a real POST /sites endpoint
commits.body:
The backend for adding a custom label class already existed
(LabelClassesView.post(), Decision 49) -- only the UI to reach it was
missing, so users were stuck with the 7 default classes.

Real gap found while wiring this up: create_label_class() requires a
site_id, but there was no way to get one without first triggering an
embed/label/paint action -- SitesView only had a GET. A user in "New
site" mode wanting custom classes before ever painting a tile had no
path to a real site id. Fixed with SitesView.post() (reuses the
already-existing embeddings_client.create_site()), and added site_id
to TaskLabelApplyView's response for the same reason.

Frontend: a "+ Add label class" button under the palette, one field
(name; color via a native color input) -- the canonical value is
slugified from the name client-side rather than typed separately.

commits.subject: Default "New site" name to the task's own name
commits.body:
Zero extra typing for the common case (a genuinely new location) while
keeping "Existing site" an equally visible, real choice for revisiting
a known place. Doesn't change the underlying site/task relationship --
site defaulting to (and staying pinned to) task would remove the whole
reason site exists separately (no two tasks would ever share a site_id,
which is what makes cross-visit comparison and pooled training
possible at all). Just a pre-filled, still-editable default.

commits.subject: Add an Eraser tool to undo a mistakenly painted label
commits.body:
Shares the exact same arm/drag/batch-submit machinery as painting
(Decision 50) via a sentinel armedLabelValue -- dragging clears
whatever label each touched tile currently has instead of setting one.

Deleting a label needed to delete the right Label Studio annotation
too, not just the local copy (otherwise WebODM and Label Studio
silently diverge). Since one Label Studio task can accumulate several
annotations across repeated repaints, generically rediscovering "which
annotation is current" at delete time was too fragile -- instead, the
exact annotation id is now tracked at creation time:

- New labels.label_studio_annotation_id column (schema change,
  schema/0003_labels_annotation_id.sql -- applied to the live Pod).
- upsert_label()/TaskLabelApplyView store the real id
  create_annotation() returns.
- label_studio_client.delete_annotation() -- real DELETE
  /api/annotations/{id}/.
- New TaskLabelClearView (POST .../labels/clear): deletes the exact
  Label Studio annotation (best-effort, doesn't block clearing local
  state on failure) then the local labels row(s).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Fix Label Studio 401: exchange PAT for a real access token before use
commits.body:
A Label Studio Personal Access Token is a JWT refresh token, not a usable
Bearer access token on its own -- sending it directly as
"Authorization: Bearer <PAT>" made every API call (create_project,
import_tasks, register_webhook) fail with a 401 "Authentication
credentials were not provided," confirmed live against
labelstudio.pods.portals.tapis.io. It must be exchanged via
POST /api/token/refresh for a short-lived access token first.

_get_access_token()/_refresh_access_token() do that exchange (cached
~5min, refreshed with a safety margin); _auth_headers() now sends the
exchanged token, and _request() retries once on a 401 in case the cached
token expired early.

commits.subject: fix: add submission lock to prevent duplicate task processing
commits.body:
If process_new_task() takes longer than the 30s Redis lock timeout
(e.g. ClusterODM retry loop = 68s), the main lock expires and a
second worker can re-enter process(), see uuid as empty, and submit
again.

Add a second Redis lock (task_submit_{id}) with nx=True and 120s
expiry around the process() call. Only one worker can hold this lock.
Degrades gracefully if Redis is unavailable.

commits.subject: feat: remove Tapis JWT refresh, treat expiry as reauthentication boundary
commits.body:
Portals tenant does not support refresh-token flow. This change removes
all refresh-token usage from WebODM's runtime and makes JWT expiry a
hard logout boundary:

- Add get_valid_access_token(): returns JWT only when locally valid
  (checks expires_at and JWT exp claim with 30s skew, no HTTP calls)
- Remove TapisOAuth2Token.refresh() and get_or_refresh_access_token()
- Remove POST /api/oauth2/tapis/refresh/{client_id}/ route
- Stop storing refresh tokens in OAuth callback (clear on login/logout)
- All callers (ClusterODM admin, task, CKAN, embeddings, upstream,
  storage) now use get_valid_access_token()
- TapisTokenManager: immediate redirect to /logout/ on expiry (no modal,
  no 10s delay), NaN expiry handling, dedup guard
- Template tag returns expired token metadata so pages can log out on
  reload-after-expiry
- Fix _decode_jwt_payload regression from refactor (dead code in
  _looks_like_jwt, decode logic lost)
- Add tests: token validity helpers, JS expiry redirect, expired JWT
  rejection in ClusterODM admin, embeddings mock updates

Design spec: docs/design/2026-08-28-tapis-jwt-expiry-logout.md

successful folder pick so users can chain through several directories
